title: Remarks at Echo, Utah
paragraphs: It is a very great pleasure to meet all of you to-day. And as I am going home to my own family, I want to pay a special word of greeting to the men and women who came here with the babies in their arms. I have enjoyed to the full my trip through Utah to-day. I am struck whenever I come into your state with your prosperity and with the evidence that it has been won primarily because of the character of your men and women. (Applause) Utah was not a country to which people afraid to work would ever have come. You did not here come in to take possession of rich, well watered valley bottoms where the hand of man has but little to do. All of the prosperity you have had has been won b y the men and women who did the work; because you applied thrift, intelligence, and water to the soil,— all three qualities. Water would not have amounted to anything without the thrift and intelligence. Because you did that you have made of this state what it is and put it upon a footing of stable and assured prosperity. I congratulate you upon the state, but I congratulate you most upon yourselves. (Cheers and applause)
